alignment.note: Greek employs an aorist middle participle (προσκαλεσάμενος, 'having summoned to himself'); the Vulgate matches with a passive participial ablative absolute (convocata turba). The Peshitta resolves the participle into a finite coordinated verb ܘܩܪܐ ('and he called'), a typical Syriac paratactic flattening of Greek subordination, and the Peshitta verb is already counted with the conjunction in this group.

The Peshitta explicitly supplies the subject ܝܫܘܥ ('Jesus'), which is only implicit in the Greek third-person verb and the Latin. This is a characteristic Syriac clarifying expansion naming the actor of the verb.
μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ / ܬܠܡܝܕܘܗܝ / discipulis suis; the Syriac fuses noun + possessive suffix into a single token.
εἶπεν / ܘܐܡܪ / dixit; the Peshitta prefixes the coordinating conjunction, consistent with its paratactic style.
αὐτοῖς / ܠܗܘܢ / eis; the Vulgate colon (idx 8) renders the Greek high-point punctuation.
εἴ / ܡܢ / Si; the Syriac uses the relative-conditional ܡܢ ܕ ('whoever') rather than a true conditional particle.

Greek τις and Latin quis express the indefinite subject 'anyone'; the Peshitta encodes this notion within the relative construction ܡܢ ܕܨܒܐ ('whoever desires') and has no separate indefinite pronoun token.

Greek reads ὀπίσω μου ἀκολουθεῖν ('to follow after me') with the verb ἀκολουθέω; the Peshitta renders ܕܢܐܬܐ ܒܬܪܝ ('to come after me') using the verb 'to come' (a-th-a) plus the adverb 'after', a Semitic idiom for discipleship. The Vulgate me sequi simplifies to the direct verb 'follow' without the spatial adverb.

Greek ἀπαρνησάσθω ('let him utterly deny') and Latin deneget render self-renunciation; the Peshitta uses the root k-p-r (ܢܟܦܘܪ), which carries the sense 'to deny, repudiate, disown' and is cognate with Hebrew כָּפַר, a slightly stronger covenantal nuance of disavowal.
ἑαυτὸν / ܒܢܦܫܗ / semetipsum; the Syriac literally reads 'in his soul/self' (n-p-sh), idiomatic for the reflexive. The Vulgate colon (idx 16) and the following Greek καί are clausal connectors.
ἀράτω τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ / ܘܢܫܩܘܠ ܙܩܝܦܗ / et tollat crucem suam; the Syriac ܙܩܝܦܗ derives from z-q-p ('to set upright, crucify') with possessive suffix, fusing 'cross' + 'his'.

Greek and Latin close with the verb 'follow' (ἀκολουθείτω μοι / sequatur me); the Peshitta again employs ܘܢܐܬܐ ܒܬܪܝ ('and let him come after me'), repeating the come-after-me discipleship idiom rather than a verb of following, maintaining internal Syriac stylistic consistency with the earlier clause.
